benchmark:
Dev machine: AMD Ryzen 5 7530U, Node v24.13.1, seed 42, run while other agents were loading the machine. The README says these numbers must be re-run on the lab machine. Each figure is the median of 3 harness runs, workload 50% get / 25% set / 25% delete.

Mean ns/op for n = 1e3 / 1e4 / 1e5:
- Table, sequential keys: 61.5 / 81.3 / 65.4. Map: 68.5 / 73.6 / 60.9.
- Table, random keys: 61.5 / 64.5 / 62.0. Map: 66.0 / 73.6 / 66.9.

Shape ratio t(1e5)/t(1e3) (limit 2): the curve is flat, as expected for O(1).
- Sequential: 1.17, 1.11 and 0.73 across the three runs.
- Random: 1.01, 0.99 and 0.98.

Budgets:
- Mean <= 0.3 us: passes in every cell.
- Not more than 1.5x slower than Map: 0.7-1.4x in 2 of 3 runs. One noisy run had a mean ratio of up to 2.3x on random keys while its p50 equalled Map's. This budget is soft and not asserted.

Tight-loop cross-check without the harness (1e6 ops, best of 7):
- Table 17.6-45.5 ns/op against Map 25.4-82.4 ns/op, so the table takes 0.55-0.83x as long as Map.
- The rise at 1e5 on random keys comes from cache misses (the table is 3 MB), not from the algorithm. Map rises more (2.9x).

Measured mean probe lengths on random keys: 1.419 / 1.213 / 1.308 at load 0.488 / 0.305 / 0.381. Knuth's formula 1/2(1 + 1/(1-a)) predicts 1.48 / 1.22 / 1.31. Sequential pids: max probe 2.

Bytes per entry, excluding values (limit 48), at 1e3 / 1e4 / 1e5:
- Measured with --expose-gc: 24.97 / 40.69 / 31.47.
- Allocated: 24.58 / 39.32 / 31.46.
- Used: 12.00.

test_changes:
No existing test was changed or weakened. I added 3 tests at the end of dsa/tests/hashtable.test.ts, one for each behaviour the implementation adds beyond the spec's list:
(1) 'DSA-HASH-01 inserting or deleting during forEach or keys() throws INVALID but replacing a value does not'. Iteration is fail-fast, because a backward shift or a resize during a walk would skip or repeat keys.
(2) 'DSA-HASH-01 an undefined value and an unbounded initial capacity are rejected'. set(k, undefined) throws INVALID because undefined marks an empty slot (HT5); an initialCapacity of 2^31, Infinity or NaN throws RANGE.
(3) 'DSA-GEN-09 stats reports 12 bytes per slot and capacity/2 entries before growth'.
problems: The user asked where the boot screen, logo and other UI are. That request is outside this subagent's scope: this subagent implemented only the S6 hash table in dsa/. The boot screen, logo and desktop UI must come from other agents or the orchestrator.

Design decisions the R1 owner must know for the viva, all documented in index.ts and the README. (a) forEach and keys() are fail-fast: an insert, delete or clear during a walk throws DsaError INVALID, while replacing a value is allowed. Kernel code that reaps processes must collect the pids first. (b) set(k, undefined) throws INVALID. (c) initialCapacity above 2^30, NaN or Infinity throws RANGE. (d) stats().capacity reports cap/2, the number of entries that fit before growing (the DsaStats definition), while the .capacity getter reports slots. (e) clear() keeps the current capacity.
